paper.title: Evolving Medical Imaging Agents via Experience-driven Self-skill Discovery
paper.central_claim: MACRO: mining recurring tool sequences from verified (correct-answer) trajectories into registered composite tools, with image-feature memory and a GRPO stage rewarding composite use, consistently improves multi-step orchestration accuracy and cross-domain generalization of a 3B medical imaging agent over static-toolchain agents.

gap.author_gap: Medical agents use predefined static tool sets/invocation strategies that are brittle under domain shift and need manual re-design.
gap.checked_gap: Plausible real limitation (fixed toolchain) but the paper presents no measurement of brittleness of static chains beyond comparing to baselines; the genuinely changed non-weight object is the tool/action registry plus memory.
gap.lineage_closest_adjacent: Voyager-style skill libraries, tool-making/ToolMaker agents, MemSkill and EvolveR (cited), Biomni (cited). Only MemSkill, EvolveR and Biomni are cited by the paper; classical skill-library and tool-creation lineages are not compared (source: paper Sec 2, version v1).
gap.residue: Generic skill-library growth already exists; the unaddressed residue is medical-domain composites validated beyond answer match.
gap.stakes: Maintenance cost and degradation when imaging protocols shift; asserted not measured.
gap.method_response: Mine frequent successful tool sequences, register as composites, reward their use.
gap.remaining_gap: Composite admission is by frequency and trajectory success only; no evidence composites are causally useful versus arbitrary usage; no cross-domain/modality shift test.
unresolved: Value of tau and number/identity of discovered composites not in text
Closest non-medical tool-library baselines not run

assessment.evidence_level_note: Both seats 'task'; kept. The memory and registry are built on training episodes and read at evaluation, and Table 3 toggles them. But REFUGE2/MITEA splits, patient separation and test-time update behaviour are unstated (index F3 unknown). So the 'later tasks' cannot be confirmed as distinct from the build stream. retained would need that split stated.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Single-run, author-reported BACC/F1 gains on REFUGE2 and MITEA (and RAM-W600 against task-specific classifiers) for a LoRA-tuned 3B agent that adds label-gated memory retrieval, frequency-mined composite tools and a composite-usage GRPO stage. The additive ablation points the same way. Cross-domain generalization, composite-level validity and the causal channel of composites at inference are not shown.
unresolved: Train/test splits for REFUGE2/MITEA and whether memory/registry update at test time.
τ, k and the composite inventory; how a composite is presented/executed at inference (opus:O01, opus:O02).

G.reason: Both seats 2; re-checked. 'Tool sets and invocation strategies are predefined and remain static' is a concrete fixed object (son55:E001), and MemSkill/EvolveR/Biomni are cited (sol:E001). General tool/skill-library growth outside medicine is not compared (son55:E014), and brittleness under shift is asserted, not measured.

M.reason: Both seats 2; re-checked. Label-gated memory, frequency-mined composites and a GRPO stage form a concrete chain. But the RL reward pays for composite presence, not correctness (son55:E002, sol:E004), frequency stands in for utility (sol:E003), and no account is given of why composites should raise diagnostic accuracy. Not refuted by the paper's own equations, so not 1.

X.reason: Both seats 2; kept, with an Opus finding added (shared correction on the reason). The write gate (correct final answer; sol:E009), mining rule (sol:E003) and image retrieval (sol:E002) are specified. τ, k, the composite inventory, retirement and versioning are not. The paper also defines a composite two ways: as an action in a growing action space (opus:O02) and, in the reward, as an atomic tool-name run inside one step (opus:O01). It never says how a composite reaches the policy at inference, including in row C (no GRPO). That is anchor 2 (key interface unclear or conflicting; precedent r12b ARISE). Not 1, because the write and read paths themselves are reconstructable.

E.measurement.reason: Both seats 2; re-checked. BACC/F1 on public labelled datasets suit imbalanced diagnosis. The RAM-W600 row and the Table 1 deltas recompute exactly (opus:O04). Gaps: no sample sizes or confusion matrices, task-specific baselines near chance (son55:E013), and two text slips (four conditions called 'three'; 'recall' claimed but never reported; opus:O03). These do not touch the metric.

E.causality.reason: Both seats 2; re-checked. There is a same-hyperparameter additive ablation A→B→C→D (sol:E005, son55:E006, son55:E007). Missing: leave-one-out arms, a hand-designed/random-composite or correctness-aware-reward control, and a stated channel for row C (counted under X, A2). Table 1 sets a per-dataset-trained agent against zero-shot VLMs and agents (unequal training exposure; A2 also E.cost).

E.holdout.reason: Both seats 1; re-checked. Only RAM-W600 names a test set. REFUGE2/MITEA splits, patient-level separation and whether memory/registry update at test time are unstated, and the cross-domain claim (son55:E012) has no transfer experiment. Not 0: the comparisons are on evaluation splits, and label-gated writes cannot grow the store from unlabeled test inputs as described.

E.statistics.reason: Both seats not_reported; re-checked. There are no sample sizes, seeds, intervals or repeated runs anywhere in §1–5, Tables 1–3 or the figure captions (A2 ladder: 0).
